questions.q: Why did Tesla leave his job with Thomas Edison?
a: He improved Edison’s generators but never shared in the money
Edison refused to let him experiment with radio waves
He was offered a prestigious teaching post back in Croatia
The laboratory burned down before he could start work
questions.why: Lesson 1 says Tesla redesigned the DC generators, saw no financial benefit, and then resigned.

questions.q: What did Tesla demonstrate to the National Electric Light Association?
a: A wireless message delivered to a person 30 feet away
A generator capable of powering all of New York
A receiver that picked up signals from Europe
A lamp that lit up without any wires attached
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes his first public demonstration of wireless technology using a spark transmitter.

questions.q: What happened to Tesla’s work after his laboratory burned down?
a: He struggled to find investors and his projects stalled
He sold his patents and retired as a wealthy man
He rebuilt the lab with Edison’s financial backing
He moved home to Croatia to teach physics
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the fire destroyed years of progress and made further investment hard to secure.

questions.q: When was Tesla finally credited with inventing radio communication?
a: Only after his death
During his 75th birthday celebration
Right after his first public demonstration
While he was still working for Edison
questions.why: Lesson 3 notes the invention was attributed to him posthumously, despite his lifelong fight for the patent.

questions.q: Which early hardships does the summary mention from Tesla’s childhood?
a: His older brother’s death and a bout of cholera
A fire that destroyed his family’s home
Being expelled from school for his ideas
An illness that left him partially deaf
questions.why: The overview describes his brother’s death, his own cholera, and a Croatian town with few opportunities.
